hook.title: The surprise tax
hook.text: You built a model $q$ of the world; reality is $p$. KL divergence is the **average extra surprise** you suffer each time you use $q$ to explain events that actually come from $p$. If your model is perfect, the tax is zero; otherwise it's positive. And since you can't average over every possible event, you **poll**: ask $T$ random people instead of the whole country and average their answers (that's Monte Carlo). A different poll gives a slightly different answer, because the estimate is itself random.
hook.recall: Remember the surprise tax: $D(p\|q)\ge0$, zero only when $q=p$. And a poll’s answer wobbles; Monte Carlo estimates are random variables.

tasks: Move $q$ until $D(p\|q)$ is as small as possible. What are $\mu_q,\sigma_q$ then?
Set $T=5$ and press *Draw new samples* ten times. Then $T=500$.
explore.takeaway: $D(p\|q)=\sum_xp(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\ge0$, equal to 0 iff $p=q$. Monte Carlo: $\hat g=\frac1T\sum_tg(x^t)$ with $x^t\sim P$ independent; $\hat g$ is random.

build.prompt: Order a Monte Carlo estimate of $\mathbb E_{x\sim P}[g(x)]$.
items: Express the quantity as $\mathbb E_{x\sim P}[g(x)]=\sum_xg(x)P(x)$
build.explanation: Slide 35: three bullets. The estimator $\hat g$ depends on the random samples, so it is a random variable.

questions.prompt: Which is a property of the KL divergence $D(p\|q)$?
questions.explanation: The surprise tax is never negative; it vanishes only for a perfect model.

questions.prompt: Monte Carlo estimate of $\mathbb E_{x\sim P}[g(x)]$:
questions.explanation: The poll: average the answers from $T$ people drawn from the population.

options: KL is the most commonly used divergence in deep generative models
The Monte Carlo estimate $\hat g$ is a deterministic number
questions.explanation: The slide asks “$\hat g$ is a random variable. Why?” Because the samples are random, a new poll gives a new $\hat g$.

questions.prompt: For 784 binary pixels there are $2^{784}\approx10^{235}$ possible images. What follows even with $10^7$ training examples?
options: Extremely sparse coverage, so the model must generalise
The model can memorise every image
questions.explanation: A poll of $10^7$ out of $10^{235}$ possibilities: nearly the whole space is unseen.

questions.prompt: *“KL divergence is a distance, so $D(p\|q)=D(q\|p)$.”* What is wrong?
options: KL is not symmetric in general: swapping $p$ and $q$ changes the value (the explorer shows two different numbers)
questions.explanation: Surprise tax depends on who is being used to explain whom. (Asymmetry is standard background, not stated on the slides.)
